XIGMA four-stage pipeline
Unified physics-parameter framework shared by the GUI and both models' own specs
Duck-typing convention adopted to resolve the ModelAdapter isinstance bug
Zero-correlation focus convention linking geometric convention, Twiss parameters, and angular divergence
Transverse and longitudinal sizes combine into the peak electron density formula
Input parameters flow through the 6D Gaussian model to produce derived output parameters
From electron-beam input parameters to derived-output quantities (energy/charge, bunch length/density, emittance/beta*)
Xigma-i pending tasks (streaming GPU, crossing angle, rename, gamma-axis rescaling)
Analytical model pending tasks (foci displacement, non-round beam yield, collimated spectrum)
Pulse energy/peak intensity jointly determined by transverse size, duration and energy input
Geometric focus offset -> Rayleigh length -> beam size/intensity at interaction point
Peak intensity (focus and interaction) chained into normalized amplitude a0
Input parameters -> intensity profile -> Rayleigh length -> a0 -> derived output pipeline
Spec completeness components: example, validation checks, and explicit out-of-scope boundary
xigma-i's gui_adapter.py as one of several pluggable ModelAdapters alongside kascade, delta, and analytical
Documented gotchas specific to the spectrum_kernel_4d GPU kernel: a0 Jacobian factor, shared-memory aliasing, dr scope
Documented deposition.py-level traps: sparse tables, float precision, CPU/GPU cell mismatch
Stage 0-1-2 tabulated pipeline data flow (particles -> deposition -> spectrum4d)
reference.py cross-checks surface both known open discrepancies
XIGMA-I code ownership (author + organization)
Canonical variables, mass-shell constraint, and the waist-sampling algorithm that enforces them
Structured fit model plus synthetic-baseline accuracy estimation via Mahalanobis distance
Waist sampling, vacuum drift, and structured fitting as the three core pipeline stages

The PhysicalQuantity/ModelSpec/adapt_to_model parameter-convention framework (io/quantities.py, io/schema.py, io/adapter.py) — fully built and demonstrated but not wired into any real GUI adapter as of this doc
